claims.disproof_condition: Re-scope the Google captive-only claim if a customer-named disclosure (vendor filing, Google statement, or teardown) ties vendor OCS shipments to Google's Apollo/TPU infrastructure; downgrade vendor OCS momentum if backlog stops growing or converts poorly in subsequent quarters.
claims.statement: Commercial (vendor) OCS demand is now material at SEC-filing grade: Lumentum's OCS backlog exceeds $400 million on extraordinary customer demand, and it received an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar CPO order deliverable 1H CY2027 — customers unnamed. Relevance to the Google/Palomar cohort: this is the concrete disproof path of the in-house-only scoping materializing — third-party analyses attribute the bulk of 2026 external OCS procurement to Google, but no vendor filing names Google, so that attribution stays tier-3 unverified. If a named disclosure ties these backlogs to Google, the captive-vs-merchant OCS demand-pool separation must be re-scoped.

source_doc.title: Lumentum Q2 FY2026 earnings release (8-K ex-99.1) — OCS backlog and CPO order

sources.quote: Our forward guidance calls for over 85 percent year-over-year revenue growth, yet we are only at the starting line for two substantial opportunities: optical circuit switches (OCS) and co-packaged optics (CPO). In OCS, we are scaling rapidly to meet extraordinary customer demand that has already driven our backlog well beyond $400 million. In CPO, we received an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar order, deliverable in first half calendar 2027.
